newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabo sets NLG 150 mln equity-linked deal for EBRD.
newsitem.headline: Rabo sets NLG 150 mln equity-linked deal for EBRD.

text.p: Rabo Securities NV said on Tuesday it was launching a 150 million guilder zero coupon bond for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) which would be linked to an index of shares in four Dutch publishing and media companies.

Rabo said it was launching a product called the "Dutch Publishers Sprinter" which combines an investment in the EBRD bond with an investment in an index made up of shares in VNU, Wolters Kluwer, PolyGram and Elsevier.
Hubert Maas of Rabo's syndication department said the EBRD zero coupon bonds would only be available to investors as part of the Sprinter package.
The product had been designed to outperform a direct investment in the underlying shares making up the index by using options to leverage up any capital gains, he said.

The Sprinter has an issue price of 101.50 percent, a maturity date of November 4, 2003 and will be listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange. Maas said its market price would be derived from the yield on seven-year Dutch government bonds and the value of the index which currently stands around 680.
Rabo said that as a result of the options leverage effect the Sprinter would give investors a return equal to 2.4 times any gains in the publishers index above a level of 800.
Investors are guaranteed a minimum repayment on maturity of 80 percent and a second guaranteed repayment level corresponding to an index value of 883.3, once that level has been reached.
When the sprinter matures investors can opt for payment in cash or in shares of the four publishers.
Maas declined to comment on whether Rabo had been buying or planned to buy shares of the four publishing and media groups to meet repayment obligations.

He said the Sprinter had been linked to publishing and media stocks because this sector had achieved an annual average return of some 26 percent over the last five years, roughly double the return on the AEX index of 25 Dutch blue chip stocks.
The product was attracting interest among both institutional and private investors in the Netherlands and some London-based fund managers had also shown interest, Maas added.
